classification.difficultyReason: Read three boundaries and their shaded sides, distinguishing strict and inclusive inequalities.

content.prompt: State the sets of inequalities which define each unshaded region.

spec.description: Unit coordinate grid; solid blue vertical boundary, dotted purple horizontal boundary and dotted green diagonal. Shaded unwanted half-planes overlap; the required region remains white.
spec.mathematics: Window -4≤x≤4, -5≤y≤4. Boundaries x=-2, y=2 and y=2x. Shade x<-2, y>2 and y<2x.
spec.answerVisibility: Boundaries and shaded regions are permanent question givens; printed answer annotations are excluded.

answer.worked:
The unshaded region is below the dotted line $y=2$, to the right of the solid line $x=-2$, and above the dotted line $y=2x$.

Therefore $y<2$, $x\ge -2$ and $y>2x$.

spec.description: Unit coordinate grid; solid purple vertical boundary, dotted blue horizontal boundary and solid orange diagonal. Unwanted half-planes overlap, leaving the required triangular region white.
spec.mathematics: Window -2≤x≤9, -5≤y≤4. Boundaries x=3, y=-2 and y=4-x. Shade x<3, y<-2 and y>4-x.
spec.answerVisibility: Boundaries and shaded regions are permanent question givens; printed answer annotations are excluded.

answer.worked:
The unshaded region is to the right of the solid line $x=3$, above the dotted line $y=-2$, and below the solid line $y=4-x$.

Therefore $x\ge 3$, $y>-2$ and $y\le 4-x$.
